Trump Subpoenas Teachers Union for Info on Pro-Palestine Students

The expansive subpoena asked the American Federation of Teachers for information related to a vandalism case against the Michigan students.

Actual Article Body:
© THE INTERCEPT

ALL RIGHTS RESERVED

The expansive subpoena asked the American Federation of Teachers headquarters for information related to a case against Michigan student protesters.

The Trump administration quietly broadened its crackdown on campus pro-Palestine protests over the summer, moving to ensnare one of the largest unions in the country in a case revolving largely around alleged incidents of vandalism.

The national headquarters of the American Federation of Teachers, or AFT, received a grand jury subpoena in August as part of an ongoing federal investigation into protests at the University of Michigan. Twelve pro-Palestine activists have been hit with felonies in the case including federal conspiracy charges mostly stemming from allegations of minor property damage and spray-painting homes of university officials.

The subpoena against the AFT, which has not been previously reported and was obtained by The Intercept, shows the administration casting a wider net in its investigation into student protesters than was previously known.

“They’re using this language around conspiracy and trying to draw in all of these different organizations.”

The Graduate Employees’ Organization, or GEO, an AFT local at the university, also received a notice to provide information and testimony to a grand jury around the same time, according to the subpoena, which was first reported by the student newspaper Michigan Daily and a full copy of which was obtained by The Intercept.

The effort to draw a powerful, liberal union into a case that revolves around spray-painting allegations represents a dramatic escalation in Donald Trump’s war on the left.
